one_liner: C++20 port of Rust tiny-skia (Skia-subset CPU rasterizer) with AVX2/NEON backends; first-party 1.2-1.9x faster than the Rust original.
what_it_does: A CPU-only 2D renderer that reimplements linebender/tiny-skia's Skia-derived algorithms in C++20: fill and stroke paths and rectangles, solid colours, linear/radial/sweep gradients, pixmap patterns, masks and blend modes into an RGBA Pixmap. The API keeps tiny-skia's object model (Pixmap, PathBuilder, Path, Paint, Transform, Stroke) with lowerCamelCase names and std::optional for fallible constructors, and adds an SVG filter module (feGaussianBlur, lighting, turbulence, morphology and others) that the Rust crate does not have. It is not a Skia or Cairo API replacement.
how_it_is_fast: Rendering goes through a port of Skia's raster pipeline (high-precision float and low-precision 16-bit stage paths) whose vector types (F32x8T, U16x16T and friends in src/tiny_skia/wide/) are hand-written for AVX2+FMA on x86-64 and NEON on ARM64, selected at compile time, with a scalar fallback. Since 2026-04-02 anti-aliased path fills use a port of Skia's Analytic Anti-Aliasing rasterizer (SkScan_AAAPath, src/tiny_skia/scan/PathAa.cpp), which computes exact edge coverage instead of the supersampled scanlines Rust tiny-skia uses. Axis-aligned anti-aliased rectangles take a dedicated fillRectAa path with no edge building.
when_to_use: A C++ program needs a small, dependency-free, BSD-licensed CPU rasterizer with Skia-style semantics (SVG-like paths, strokes, gradients, patterns, masks), for example SVG rendering, thumbnails or offscreen chart output.
You are porting Rust tiny-skia or resvg-style rendering code to C++ and want output that matches the Rust crate within a golden-image tolerance.
ARM64 / Apple Silicon targets, where the project's own numbers show the largest gain over Rust tiny-skia (README 1.4-1.9x; later calibrated baselines 2.9-3.5x).
You need SVG filter primitives (blur, colour matrix, lighting, displacement, turbulence) in C++ without pulling in a browser engine or Skia.
when_not_to_use: Maximum CPU rendering throughput: it is measured only against Rust tiny-skia, which its own README puts 20-100% slower than Skia on x86-64 and 100-300% slower on ARM; on the independent bl_bench M1 Pro run, Blend2D, Vello CPU and the JUCE renderer (3.09x Rust tiny-skia, derived from page data) are far ahead of Rust tiny-skia, and none of them has been compared with this port.

Portable x86-64 binaries: the native target is compiled with -mavx2 -mfma (CMake and Bazel) with no runtime dispatch, so it faults on CPUs without AVX2 and FMA (the author's Donner issue #1286 says this of the vendored copy); ship the tiny_skia_scalar target or per-ISA builds instead.
Text rendering: like Rust tiny-skia (whose README lists text as the main missing feature), the drawing API is fillRect, fillPath, strokePath, drawPixmap and applyMask only.
You need bit-exact Rust tiny-skia output: analytic AA and other changes make it near-pixel-accurate only.

Low risk tolerance: 9 stars, one maintainer with many commits co-authored by an AI assistant, no tagged releases seen, and an out-of-bounds pixel write in the anti-aliased blitter fixed only on 2026-07-04 (PR #30).

integration.dependencies: none at runtime; the tests and benchmarks use GoogleTest, Google Benchmark and a Rust toolchain (rules_rust) for the tiny-skia FFI cross-checks
integration.min_toolchain: C++20; GCC 11+, Clang 14+ or MSVC 19.30+ (CONTRIBUTING); Bazel 7+ or CMake 3.16+
integration.platforms: x86-64 (native target requires AVX2+FMA), ARM64 (NEON), any other target via the scalar library; CI builds Bazel on Ubuntu and CMake on Ubuntu and macOS, with no Windows CI
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same object model and algorithms as Rust tiny-skia (Pixmap, PathBuilder, Paint, Transform) in C++ naming, so Rust call sites port mechanically, but it is a C++ library, not a crate, and its output is not bit-exact

gotchas: SIMD backend is chosen at compile time: link tiny_skia (native) or tiny_skia_scalar deliberately, and on x86 the native build assumes AVX2+FMA on every target machine.

Versions before PR #30 (merged 2026-07-04) could read or write one pixel past the pixmap in RasterPipelineBlitter::blitAntiH2/blitAntiV2 when an anti-aliased edge touched the right or bottom edge; use a later commit.
Anti-aliased fillPath uses Skia's analytic AA, not Rust tiny-skia's supersampling, so edge pixels differ slightly from the Rust crate; the golden-image tests compare with a tolerance.
The library compiles with -ffp-contract=off; if you vendor the sources into a build without it (or with -ffast-math), float rounding may drift from the golden images (inference from the build files).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over Rust tiny-skia when the host program is C++ and you want the same rendering model with native SIMD and SVG filters; pick Blend2D or AGG instead when raw speed or a long track record matters, since this port has never been measured against them, Skia or Cairo.
verified_claims_summary: First-party Google Benchmark runs (RenderPerfBench.cpp, 5 repetitions, mean real time) of one 512x512 anti-aliased FillRect and one FillPath, C++ AVX2+FMA or NEON build against Rust tiny-skia 0.12.0 called through FFI, on unnamed Apple Silicon and Intel/AMD machines with an unstated compiler: README 1.9x/1.3x (FillRect, ARM/x86) and 1.4x/1.2x (FillPath). The README chart matches the 2026-03-03 calibration in run_render_perf_regression_test.sh (arm64 1.42 FillPath, 1.91 FillRect; x86 1.18 and 1.29) and was never updated; later arm64 calibrations rose to 2.00/2.80 (2026-03-05) and 2.90/3.50 (2026-04-02), so the ARM numbers are stale rather than contradicted, while the x86 side still compares AVX2+FMA C++ with SSE2-only Rust.
status_note: Active but small (156 commits, 9 stars, last author commit 2026-07-04, then only renovate[bot] dependency PRs); BSD-3-Clause and dependency-free so easy to vendor, and the author also vendors it as the default CPU renderer in jwmcglynn/donner (third_party/tiny-skia-cpp), whose copy already adds a wasm simd128 backend the standalone repo lacks.
measurement_notes: Three flaws behind the catalogued numbers, none invalidating: (1) each timed iteration also clears the 1 MiB pixmap, via memset in C++ (Pixmap::fill with a transparent colour) but a per-pixel store loop in Rust tiny-skia 0.12 (Pixmap::fill), so part of the gap can come from the clear rather than rasterization (size not measured); (2) since 2026-04-02 FillPath compares Skia analytic AA in C++ against supersampled AA in Rust, an algorithm change rather than a like-for-like port speedup; (3) the regression guard that holds the calibrated ratios is skipped in CI, because CI runs bazel test //... without -c opt and the script exits early unless the compilation mode is opt. Neither benchmark shape touches the pixmap edge, so the PR #30 out-of-bounds bug does not affect the numbers.
